item.title: all agentic architectures
item.description:
## The Problem
Modern agentic systems often struggle with the reliability of LLM-as-scorer mechanisms, where probabilistic free-text outputs lead to inconsistent agent behavior—colloquially known as the "flat-band pathology." This repository addresses that instability by implementing a deterministic-picker pattern, requiring LLMs to commit to categorical features (booleans, enums) rather than unstructured scores, allowing Python to compose the final decision signal.

item.title: mimic
item.description:
**The Problem** When a mobile or web app hits a protected API, each request carries a bundle of static credentials (bearer token, device ID, session cookie). Capturing this traffic once and replaying it is the fastest way to get an API client without reverse‑engineering the app. Developers still need a mechanism to record traffic, extract the auth bundle, and generate a usable Python library that can be imported and called like any other module.

item.title: samsung tv root
item.description:
## The Problem Home‑owner developers need a reliable, local‑host tool to keep Samsung Tizen TVs in a developer‑mode state, remap remote input, and gain temporary root for diagnostics. Existing vendor tools are closed, fragile, and lack repeatability. This repo supplies a portable, open‑source suite that performs the same volatile‑root workflow on two specific TV models (QN90B and QN90F) and exposes a CLI for day‑to‑day use.

item.title: inferssd
item.description:
## The Problem Running mixture‑of‑experts (MoE) models that exceed a system’s RAM or VRAM is impractical on commodity hardware. Existing inference engines either refuse to load such models or require expensive GPUs or large memory budgets. A solution that streams the inactive experts from SSD while keeping the active slice in memory would unlock large‑scale inference on laptops and small servers.

item.description:

The result is long warm‑up times, high memory usage, and uneven load distribution.

item.title: remoto.el
item.description:
## The Problem
Browsing a GitHub repository usually means cloning it first. That costs disk space, creates directory clutter, and breaks flow when you only need to check a function signature or read a README. `remoto.el` removes that friction by making remote repos browsable directly in Emacs, as if they were local directories.

item.title: omnigraph
item.description:

Existing graph engines either lock the entire graph for writes, lack branching semantics, or store data in a proprietary format that ties compute to storage.

item.title: lot map
item.description:

A visual, real‑time map would let developers see the flow of work and spot bottlenecks instantly.
